name: Ambrym
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Paton, W.F. 1971. Ambrym (Lonwolwol) Grammar. Pacific Linguistics Series B-19. Canberra: Australian National University.
catalog_locator: p.12, par. 2 'Syllables and Accent' (PDF page 24 of sealang)
catalog_quote: SYLLABLES AND ACCENT 2. Syllables may begin or end with either vowels or consonants; e.g., na? what?; nal, road; gami, you all; awa, rope; nɔrnɔr, think. There is no apparent rule or uniformity of accent. Some words are distinguished only by difference of accent, e.g., bíhi, to bind; bihí, a cave. The pronunciation of each word is an individual matter.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage is verbatim at Paton 1971 p.12 par.2 (p.24) in the sealang and page scan we hold. (2) Deciding source: Paton 1971 is the sole grammar of Lonwolwol in Glottolog and the only description found; it is a posthumously published 1956 missionary dissertation with an impressionistic phonology, so the 'lexical / no rule' coding rests on a three-sentence statement plus one minimal pair. (3) The 1973 dictionary (downloaded now, open) marks accent on the bíhi/bihí pair, confirming the contrast is real and lexically recorded; it adds no rule. No newer Lonwolwol phonology, JIPA illustration, or dissertation was located (von Prince/DoBeS West Ambrym work covers Daakaka, Daakie, Dalkalaen, not Lonwolwol); (4) Status 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced': best available source is held and quoted

sources.citation: Paton, W.F. 1973. Ambrym (Lonwolwol) Dictionary. Pacific Linguistics C-21. Canberra: Australian National University. xiv+346 pp. (open, CC BY-SA, sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/)
sources.quote: No prose statement on accent. Accent is marked with an acute on headwords where it is distinctive: bíhi¹ 'to bind' (first syllable) vs bihí² 'a cave' (second syllable); North Ambrym comparanda given as 'bíhi, and: bihí'. Most headwords carry no accent mark.
sources.locator: front matter pp.iii-ix (no accent statement; key to phonetic symbols lists no stress mark); p.15 (p.29) headwords bíhi¹ (v.i.t.) 'to bind, bind up' vs bihí² 'a cave, hole in cliff' (crop saved)
sources.note: Only other primary Lonwolwol source; its accent-marked headwords (bíhi¹ vs bihí²) independently attest the lexical minimal pair our classification rests on. downloaded and checked now.
